claims.statement: The single anthropic-oauth-proxy binary assembles the Tokio/Axum proxy and optional in-process admin server, while the Tailscale Operator owns tailnet exposure outside the pod.
The binary initializes JSON logging using LOG_LEVEL, then RUST_LOG, then info as fallback, and installs the Prometheus recorder before serving.
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT enables a separate batched OTLP gRPC tracer; the Prometheus recorder and scrape route are present independently.
Config path selection loads one TOML file: --config <path> overrides CONFIG_PATH, which overrides the relative default anthropic-oauth-proxy.toml.
CREDENTIAL_FILE overrides oauth.credential_file after deserialization only when [oauth] is present; it neither creates the section nor waives the required TOML field.

A present [oauth] selects OAuth pool mode and causes nonempty [[headers]] to be cleared with a warning before header syntax validation. With no [oauth], passthrough is selected even without static headers.

Startup requires readable, deserializable TOML with the required proxy address and upstream URL; config validation rejects unparseable or non-HTTP(S) URLs, zero proxy timeout or concurrency, invalid active static headers, and an empty credential path or zero cooldown or refresh settings in OAuth mode.
The binary builds a reusable reqwest client with a five-second connection timeout, distinct from the configurable timeout passed to the proxy handler.
Passthrough applies configured static headers without overriding Authorization, does not rewrite the request body, and does not participate in account failover.
OAuth startup loads the JSON credential store and initializes a missing file as an empty store; reading, parsing, or initializing the store unsuccessfully aborts startup.

The OAuth startup pool is seeded from oauth.providers when nonempty and all stored account IDs otherwise, and is shared by the OAuth provider and a proactive refresh task that periodically checks for near-expiry tokens.
OAuth max_failover_attempts is fixed from the initial list size with a floor of one; runtime enrollment changes pool membership but does not resize the proxy's request attempt budget.

Provider is the extension boundary for whether the proxy parses request JSON, request preparation, upstream error classification and reporting, and provider-specific health, rather than the Axum router choosing credentials.
AnthropicOAuthProvider selects a pool account, removes client Authorization and x-api-key, injects the selected Bearer token and provider headers, and modifies the JSON body during preparation.

The committed tailnet route is the Tailscale-class Ingress with a TLS host and prefix / to the unannotated proxy ClusterIP Service on port 80, whose named http target is the proxy pod's port 8080; forwarded data requests go to the configured Anthropic HTTPS upstream.

GET /health and GET /metrics are local routes on the proxy listener, reachable through the same Ingress prefix and outside the fallback's max_connections concurrency limiter; /metrics renders Prometheus text.
The Deployment uses /health on the proxy port for startup, readiness, and liveness probes and annotates the pod for Prometheus to scrape /metrics on port 8080.

The health handler returns HTTP 200 with JSON provider status, mode, uptime, counters and optional pool details; it is not an upstream reachability or account-availability probe, so an empty OAuth pool can report unhealthy with 200 while a valid proxied request fails preparation with 503.

Admin account and pool inspection, PKCE enrollment, and removal use a separate unauthenticated application router with the live OAuth pool, reached through a separate admin ClusterIP Service and pod listener on 9090, not the Ingress backend. The proxy router does not mount the admin handlers.
The operator runbook directs account-management callers to use kubectl port-forward rather than the tailnet Ingress.

The separate admin task only starts in OAuth mode with admin.enabled set to true, which defaults to false; the default bind address is 0.0.0.0:9090, and admin bind failure logs an error without aborting the proxy.

The committed Kustomize deployment loads generated ConfigMap TOML from a read-only mount via CONFIG_PATH, enables both OAuth and admin, and uses the credentials PVC at /data for /data/credentials.json with an empty providers list and ignored static header settings.
The committed Deployment uses one replica, the Recreate update strategy, and a six-second pod termination grace period.

Ingress-only exposure supersedes the sidecar and Service-annotation models: the addendum documents a duplicate tailnet hostname conflict when Service annotations and Ingress coexisted, while the committed pod has no tailscaled sidecar and neither Service carries Tailscale exposure annotations.

main uses the I/O-free service state model on startup: ConfigLoaded yields Starting and StartListener, a failed main listener bind aborts startup, and successful bind dispatches ListenerReady to enter Running.

The model's Running-to-Draining-to-Stopped transitions describe shutdown and its redundant-signal or timeout behavior but are not dispatched by main; request events are no-ops in the model and proxy handlers track counters directly.

At runtime SIGINT or Unix SIGTERM triggers a one-shot Axum graceful shutdown notification; main bounds its wait for the proxy task to drain with a five-second timeout started after the signal, not at server startup.

The proxy handler's in-flight count is logged when the drain deadline is exceeded and is not a shutdown gate; its guard drops on handler return even if an Axum streaming response body is still active.

The admin server and proactive refresh task are not included in the proxy server drain; after the drain wait main separately shuts down the optional tracer provider to flush spans under the exporter's own timeout.
Focused config tests cover CLI-over-env path selection, validation failures, OAuth precedence, and the credential path override.

Focused router tests exercise monitoring with a slow upstream and a single proxy slot, check that OAuth health includes pool details, and check that an admin-router request to /v1/messages returns 404 without involving Ingress.
Service state-model tests directly exercise drain timeout, redundant shutdown and terminal Stopped transitions rather than sending OS signals or exercising the exporter.
